__baseline_prompt__.text: A photographic space-horror scene: a woman whose facial appearance and short dark bob are guided by the supplied portrait stands in an unsettling encounter inside the listening nursery of a living spacecraft. The supplied portrait guides her face and hair, while her work clothes and surroundings belong to this invented scene. Her large brown eyes, delicate oval face and wispy dark fringe remain recognizable in a clear three-quarter view. She wears a pale gray expedition coverall with a small amber work lamp at the sternum. Her lips are slightly parted as she looks down toward the nearest organism, her unguarded face warm and human against the chamber. She has stopped halfway through a careful step on a narrow maintenance landing. Her left boot is planted flat on the deck; her right boot hovers a few centimeters above it, knee softly bent. Her left hand grips the waist-high rail beside her, and her right hand stays close against her chest. The interrupted movement reads as a person suddenly realizing that this place can notice her. The inner hull forms broad pale cartilage arches joined by taut semitranslucent membranes with branching dark vessels. A manufactured circular porthole is set into one living arch, its bolted metal ring clasped by the membrane; through it, a sparse star field and the hard white edge of a distant moon establish the spacecraft's exterior. The deck and arch membranes meet in continuous grown folds, giving the structure the material continuity of an organ rather than decoration applied to a room. Beside the landing, a shallow black nursery pool supports a small colony of unfamiliar sail organisms. Each has a dark knotted holdfast fixed to the pool bed, a thin stalk and a broad translucent fan with fine radiating ribs. Three large near fans curve toward the woman's hovering boot, their wet edges close to the landing; two distant fans remain upright deeper in the pool. Tiny pale cilia form a fringe at the near holdfasts. These are separate organisms living within the vessel, distinct from the large structural hull arches. Her hovering boot, the nearest bending fans and their rooted bases are visible together across one diagonal gap. Compose a landscape 3:2 photograph from the landing at a slightly low three-quarter viewpoint. Her full figure fills the left foreground, the nearest colony fills the lower right, and the porthole stays readable above the pool. The amber lamp illuminates her face and catches the organisms' ribbed translucency; cold diffused blue from the porthole separates the hull membranes. Controlled shadows retain the stalks, holdfasts and rail grip. Detailed photographic skin, worn fabric, wet thin membranes and mineral residue give the impossible habitat convincing physical presence. The dominant feeling is the quiet instant before she dares lower her foot.
